news_summary: A historic milestone in international space collaboration is underway as a Pakistani astronaut prepares to become the first foreign visitor to China’s space station.

articles.title: Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station
articles.summary: Nature, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03829-yMuhammad Zeeshan Ali is flying this week to the Tiangong module aboard a Chinese spacecraft.
articles.content:
Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

“My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He said that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, says Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

On-board research

Shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, said Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts currently on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration

Ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

According to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang said.

This event has broad significance for space exploration, international collaboration, and scientific research, including biotechnology experiments and human adaptation studies in space. articles.personality_title: Pakistani astronaut to visit China’s space station for the first time
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – China has been developing its own space station called Tiangong, or 'heavenly palace.' Until now, only Chinese astronauts, called taikonauts, have visited the station.

**What happened** – On November 25, 2026, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, will travel to the Tiangong space station aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft. He will join two Chinese taikonauts and stay for about a week before returning to Earth. Ali has trained for seven months in China, including learning Mandarin, and will carry out scientific experiments during the mission.

**Impact** – This is the first time a foreign astronaut will visit China’s space station, marking a big step for Pakistan’s space program and international cooperation. Pakistan will conduct biotechnology experiments in space, helping scientists learn how the human body adapts to spaceflight. For China, it shows how their space program is growing and opening up to partners worldwide.

**What's next step** – Ali’s mission could lead to more international collaborations on Tiangong. The scientific results from the experiments may help improve space travel and health research. China plans to continue expanding its space station and involve more countries in future missions.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Pakistan’s first astronaut is joining China’s space station, marking a milestone in international space cooperation and scientific research.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un astronaute pakistanais visite pour la première fois la station spatiale chinoise
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – La Chine développe sa propre station spatiale appelée Tiangong, ou « palais céleste ». Jusqu’à présent, seuls des astronautes chinois, appelés taïkonautes, y ont séjourné.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le 25 novembre 2026, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, pilote militaire pakistanais, se rendra à la station spatiale Tiangong à bord du vaisseau chinois Shenzhou-24. Il sera accompagné de deux taïkonautes chinois et restera environ une semaine avant de revenir sur Terre. Ali s’est entraîné sept mois en Chine, y compris en apprenant le mandarin, et réalisera des expériences scientifiques pendant la mission.

**Impact** – C’est la première fois qu’un astronaute étranger visite la station spatiale chinoise, ce qui marque une étape importante pour le programme spatial pakistanais et la coopération internationale. Le Pakistan mènera des expériences en biotechnologie dans l’espace, aidant à mieux comprendre comment le corps humain s’adapte au vol spatial. Pour la Chine, cela montre l’expansion de son programme spatial et son ouverture à des partenaires mondiaux.

**Prochaine étape** – La mission d’Ali pourrait ouvrir la voie à davantage de collaborations internationales sur Tiangong. Les résultats scientifiques aideront à améliorer les voyages spatiaux et la recherche sur la santé. La Chine prévoit d’élargir sa station spatiale et d’impliquer plus de pays dans ses futures missions.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le premier astronaute pakistanais rejoint la station spatiale chinoise, un jalon dans la coopération spatiale internationale et la recherche scientifique.
articles.personality_title_es: Astronauta paquistaní visitará por primera vez la estación espacial china
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – China está desarrollando su propia estación espacial llamada Tiangong, o 'palacio celestial'. Hasta ahora, solo astronautas chinos, llamados taikonautas, han visitado la estación.

**Qué pasó** – El 25 de noviembre de 2026, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, piloto militar paquistaní, viajará a la estación espacial Tiangong a bordo de la nave china Shenzhou-24. Irá acompañado de dos taikonautas chinos y permanecerá cerca de una semana antes de regresar a la Tierra. Ali se ha entrenado durante siete meses en China, incluyendo el aprendizaje del mandarín, y realizará experimentos científicos durante la misión.

**Impacto** – Esta es la primera vez que un astronauta extranjero visita la estación espacial china, un gran paso para el programa espacial de Pakistán y la cooperación internacional. Pakistán llevará a cabo experimentos en biotecnología en el espacio, ayudando a los científicos a entender cómo el cuerpo humano se adapta al vuelo espacial. Para China, muestra el crecimiento de su programa espacial y su apertura a socios internacionales.

**Qué sigue** – La misión de Ali podría abrir la puerta a más colaboraciones internacionales en Tiangong. Los resultados científicos podrían mejorar los viajes espaciales y la investigación en salud. China planea continuar expandiendo su estación espacial e involucrar a más países en futuras misiones.

**Frase clave** – El primer astronauta paquistaní se une a la estación espacial china, marcando un hito en la cooperación espacial internacional y la investigación científica.
